issue.title: tui3, provider, config, manual: the word is provider, everywhere a person reads

repository.name: CodeAF
repository.description: Open-Source Software factory for Open Models

issue.body:
## The ruling

Issue #1023, item 1, ruled 2026-09-14: **the person-facing word for the thing behind a model that answers a request is `provider`.** One model id is served by many machines; this surface called one of them a *lane* while the wire, OpenRouter's own refusals (`provider.only`) and the owner all said provider. Items 2–5 of #1023 are not in this pull request.

Vocabulary only. `internal/lane`, `LanePin`, `laneAutoSaid`, `lanes.go`, `lanes.json` and the `lane.talk` / `lane.guard` settings keys are unchanged — a name a person never reads costs nothing to leave alone, and renaming a key on disk would move somebody's pin.

## Every respelled string, old → new

**`internal/tui3/settings.go`**

| old | new |
| --- | --- |
| row label `lane` | `provider` |
| `lane · <model>` (the fold's own sheet label) | `provider · <model>` |
| `↑↓ move · → or tab lanes · enter choose · esc cancel · type to filter` | `… → or tab providers …` |
| routing `about`: "one model is served by many **endpoints** … no pinned **lane** … a pinned **lane** … no **machine** to name" | … many **providers** … no pinned **provider** … a pinned **provider** … no **provider** to name |
| speed guard `about`: "asked of the next-best **machine**" | "next-best **provider**" |
| prompt profile `about`: "for an **endpoint** that reports a window" | "for a **provider** that reports a window" |
| fallback models `about`: "when no **endpoint** will take the request" | "no **provider** will take the request" |

**`internal/tui3/palette.go`**

| old | new |
| --- | --- |
| `filter · ↑↓ · → lanes · ctrl+t effort · ctrl+r refresh · enter · esc` | `… → providers …` |
| `→ lanes · enter switch · esc` | `→ providers · enter switch · esc` |
| `tab lanes · enter switch · esc` | `tab providers · enter switch · esc` |
| `no machine has been measured for this model yet — machines show up after its first answer` | `no provider has been measured for this model yet — providers show up after its first answer` |
| `auto` row `about` (simple): "which **machine behind your model answers you** … a **lane** you pin is the whole request" | "which **provider answers your model** … a **provider** you pin …" |
| `auto` row `about` (latency/price): "which **machine behind your model answers you**" | "which **provider answers your model**" |

`pickerKeysFold` / `pickerKeysFoldTab` / `pickerKeysUnpin` are unchanged — they were already `enter choose · ← back · esc` and `enter unpin · ← back · esc`.

**`internal/tui3/lanes.go`** — `<host> owns the lane · change it on that machine` → `owns the provider …`; `lane · <name>` / `lane · auto` / `lane · openrouter` notes → `provider · …`.

**`internal/tui3/phase.go`** — `all lanes slow` → `all providers slow`.

**`internal/provider`**

| old | new |
| --- | --- |
| `PhaseAllSlow` = `all lanes slow` | `all providers slow` |
| `that lane went quiet — this answer is coming from another one` | `that provider went quiet — …` |
| `still no answer — trying another lane · /model switches` | `… trying another provider · /model switches` |
| `pinned lane <x> was silent for …` | `pinned provider <x> was silent for …` |
| `every lane tried` | `every provider tried` |
| `<host> does not take a lane choice; …` | `… does not take a provider choice; …` |
| `… so aforge is choosing its machine for a while` | `… choosing its provider for a while` |
| `[an attachment was removed: no endpoint serving this model could accept it]` | `… no provider serving this model …` |
| `no endpoint can serve <model> — refused after …` | `no provider can serve <model> — …` |

`RetiredPinLine` / `RetiredPinTail` and the stall offer (`coreweave is slow · switch to auto? (y)`) are unchanged — both name the provider by its own name.

**`internal/config/settings.go`** — registry row `Label: "lane"` → `"provider"`; its hint `which machine behind your model answers requests from this home … a dozen endpoints …` → `which provider answers your model, for requests from this home … a dozen providers …`; the `routing` hint's `endpoint`/`lane`/`machine` and the speed-guard and prompt-profile hints likewise.

**Manual (`internal/manual/chat/`)** — `lanes.md` keeps its file name (a page name is a stable id). Its `#` title is now `Providers — which provider answers your model, and the question a slow one asks`, and every `##` heading and sentence says provider. Swept the same way: `models-and-cost.md` (the whole *Choose a provider* / *Which provider answers* region, the two settings blocks, the fold table), `commands.md`, `keys.md`, `screen.md`, `debug-record.md`, `services.md`, `getting-started.md` (it quotes the rescue notice), `running-on-another-machine.md`. Untouched: every `lane` that means a *parallel worker slot* or the *dim lane* a line is drawn in (`tasks.md`, `saved-shapes-of-work.md`, `questions.md`, `how-tasks-run.md`, `keeping-an-eye.md`, `adaptive-runs.md`, `standing-orders.md`, `sessions-and-rewind.md`), and `docs/changes/unreleased/`, which is history.

**Retrieval.** The old words are kept as search keys so a person who still types them lands on the page: one paragraph at the top of `lanes.md` (`The word is provider. Earlier builds called the same thing a lane …`) and a handful of headings — `(this used to be called the lane)`, `Pinning one provider yourself (pinning a lane)`, `a machine that cannot take tool calls`, `a machine that will not serve my model`, `all providers slow, which older builds spelled all lanes slow`, `Providers (lanes) on a custom base URL`, `the lane I pinned`, `endpoint routing, lane routing, all the same row`.

**`docs/CHAT-V3.md`** — one sentence describing the shipped `simple` row.

## One behaviour change, and it is the word's own cost

`→ lanes` is four cells wider as `→ providers`, and four cells is exactly what `ctrl+r refresh` had bought from `enter · esc` in the placeholder's ranked tail. So **on a sixty-cell frame the `/model` box now reads `filter · ↑↓ · → providers · ctrl+t effort`** and names the refresh key from about sixty-four columns up. Spelling it `ctrl+r` alone would fit it back in and break the older law in the same comment — the keys go WHOLE, and a box saying `ctrl+r` with no word teaches nobody what the key does — so the ladder gives up the key it can no longer say properly. Both readings are pinned in `TestTheRefreshKeyIsNamedInThePlaceholderAndTheEmptyList` now, the narrow one and the whole line at eighty cells. Worth a look if you would rather buy the key back by re-ranking the fields.

## Deliberately NOT renamed

- `internal/lane`, `LanePin`, `laneAutoSaid`, `laneRowTail`, `lanes.go`, `lanes.json`, `lanes.log`.
- `lane.talk`, `lane.talk.borrow`, `lane.guard` — config keys, read and written exactly as today.
- **The `lane` key `/status --json` prints** (`internal/tui3/statusdeck.go`). It is a key a script was promised, so it stays a machinery name; the law below records it as the one exception and `lanes.md` now says on the `/status` line that this row keeps the old word and why. Worth a follow-up decision on #1023.
- `@morph` / `via morph` chip spellings, `machine` where it means a computer (`--host`, the far machine), and `endpoint` where it names OpenRouter's own `/endpoints` page, `relaxed the endpoint filter`, `No endpoints found` and `0 endpoints out of 1 requested are` (the router's own text).

## The law

`internal/tui3/providerword_law_test.go` parses every non-test file in `internal/tui3` with `go/parser` and fails on any string literal carrying the standalone word `lane`/`lanes`, with import paths cut out by shape and the `/status --json` key as the single named exception. It imports `go/ast`, so `scripts/laws.sh` picks it up and it rides `make test-laws` on every pull request.

## Needles followed, and the one probe the page had to be fixed for

`internal/e2e/tuiwords_test.go`: `phaseAllSlowWord` `all lanes slow` → `all providers slow`. Unit needles updated for the respelled strings: `internal/tui3/modelrefresh_test.go`, `lanes_test.go`, `keys_test.go`, `retrying_test.go`, `lanewalk_test.go`; `internal/session/hedge_replacement_view_test.go`; `internal/provider/prefcarry_test.go`; and the services-page sentence asserted in `internal/manual/chat_test.go`.

**No probe question was changed.** One probe did start missing, and the PAGE was fixed: making `provider` a common word in the corpus cost `services.md` the one question that is really about a key — *"how do I add an api key for another provider"* landed on `getting-started`. Its heading is now `## Add a key — connect a service, add an api key for another provider, use a different model service`, and the first sentence carries the asker's words too. Every other probe, including the lane-worded ones (`what does all lanes slow still waiting mean`, `I pinned a lane but I am on a proxy`, `does aforge do use the lane I pinned`, `the model picker says no machine has been measured for this model yet`, `a machine will not serve my model`, `how do I turn off endpoint routing`), still reaches the page.

## Evidence

Laptop: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l internal/ cmd/` all clean.

Spark (`~/af-provider`, detached at this head, tmux `af-provider`, log `~/af-provider.log`):

```
BUILD_EXIT=0
LAWS_EXIT=0          # laws: 113 files in 25 packages
PRREADY_EXIT=0       # test-quick + touched packages, -count=1
```

The touched-package run covers `cmd/aforge`, `internal/config`, `internal/e2e`, `internal/manual`, `internal/provider` (71s), `internal/session` (196s) and `internal/tui3` (~310s) — all `ok`.

**A real drive, `bin/aforge` in tmux on Spark** (`~/af-provider-drive.sh`; captures in `spark:~/af-provider-evidence/`):

```
Session Context Workspace Display Spending Safety Tasks Providers Connections
 Providers
 routing                                                        simple
    one model is served by many providers. simple is the one it ships with
    and sends no preference of ours — no pinned provider … no provider to name.
 provider                                                          auto
 speed guard                                                         on
```

```
› filter · ↑↓ · → providers · ctrl+t effort · ctrl+r refresh · enter · esc
  deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash                    $0.089/$0.18 per M · 1M · elo 1220
›   ● auto            openrouter's own routing; aforge stays out · recommended
      wafer                       0.5s · 82 t/s · $0.25/M · tail 3s · 100%
      …
─ … ─────────────────────────────── enter choose · ← back · esc · crew balanced ─
```

and the fallback row reads `where a conversation goes when no provider will take the request`. A grep for the retired word over all nine captures: **`no capture says lane`**.

## Not verified

The tmux e2e suite (`make test-e2e-tui`) was not run — this change touches needles it waits for, so it is worth one run before promotion. `--host` was not driven. The `/status --json` `lane` key is left standing and is a decision, not an oversight.

body: Item 1 shipped: #1027 (dev f08201024) — the person-facing word is **provider** everywhere (settings row, `→ providers` hints, fold sentences, rescue/stall notices, config hints, manual page *Providers*), with a tui3 law test against the word lane in string literals. Kept as-is: code identifiers, `lane.talk` keys, the `@morph` chip, and the `/status --json` `lane` key as a script contract. Items 2–5 (Settings points at /model, `→ providers` tail on the model row, `figures: openrouter` in the fold foot, no teach) remain open for the owner's call.
